overview: Russia is the largest country in the world by area, stretching across Eastern Europe and northern Asia. Its capital and largest city is Moscow. Russia was the largest republic of the Soviet Union, which broke up in 1991, and it is one of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council. Since 2014 Russia has occupied parts of Ukraine, and in 2022 it launched a full-scale invasion of the country.

geography.text: Russia spans 11 time zones, from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific Ocean. The Ural Mountains separate European Russia, where most people live, from Siberia, a vast region of forest, frozen tundra and great rivers such as the Ob, the Yenisei and the Lena. Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake in the world, and the Volga is the longest river in Europe.

history.text: Russia grew from the medieval state of Kievan Rus' and the later Grand Duchy of Moscow into a vast empire stretching to the Pacific. The tsars were overthrown in 1917, and the Bolsheviks created the Soviet Union, which lost tens of millions of people in the Second World War and became a superpower. When the Soviet Union broke up in 1991, Russia became its successor state.

events.title: Christianity adopted
events.text: Grand Prince Volodymyr of Kyiv adopts Orthodox Christianity.

events.title: First tsar
events.text: Ivan IV, 'the Terrible', is crowned tsar.

events.title: St Petersburg founded
events.text: Peter the Great builds a new capital on the Baltic.

events.title: Revolution
events.text: The tsar is overthrown and the Bolsheviks seize power.

events.title: Soviet Union breaks up
events.text: The fifteen Soviet republics become independent.
